answerability.question: Are previous Symbiknow document versions kept using Git?

evidence.text:
Symbiknow
Sample tool arguments
Single and bulk operations both use a
```
files
```
array. Preserve the UUID request ID when retrying an upload. Supply
```
document_id
```
to update a document; otherwise the request ID determines a stable new identity. Identical files with different upload request IDs retain independent identities. Identical updates still get new versions.
```
{
  "name": "upload",
  "arguments": {
    "files": [{
      "filename": "notes.txt",
      "mime_type": "text/plain",
      "source": "/notes/notes.txt",
      "request_id": "6be4ba0b-38ac-4b51-9ec1-1d4f1896857d",
      "content_base64": "SGVsbG8gU3ltYmlrbm93Cg=="
    }]
  }
}
```
Updates may include
```
expected_version: "v1"
```
for optimistic concurrency. A replay of a committed request returns the original version even after later updates. Reusing that request ID with different bytes or metadata is an error.
```
{"name":"download","arguments":{"files":[{"document_id":"DOCUMENT_ID","version":"v1"}]}}
```
Downloads include actual
```
content_base64
```
, original filename/MIME/source, the pinned version, whole-file SHA-256, range offset, returned size, and EOF. Continue ranges using that returned version. Use
```
history: true
```
on a download item to list all version metadata along with the requested byte range.
```
{"name":"search","arguments":{"query":"What did we decide?","mode":"hybrid","limit":8,"evaluate":true}}
```

Symbiknow
Processing and recovery
Original bytes are committed before conversion/model initialization. The single ingestion worker reconciles committed OCFL heads with LanceDB metadata after startup and when uploads arrive. Indexing retries replace derived chunks, never create file versions. Publication follows complete chunk writes. Search verifies hits against current OCFL heads and excludes old content while a newer version is pending.
Search reports worker activity, queued upload items, and known retry counts, rather than a complete stored-file count. Download reports the requested version's indexing status. Superseded relationship endpoints are omitted; affected linked sources are queued for fresh organization when an update is indexed.
Markdown, UTF-8 TXT, HTML, PDFs, and common image formats are supported. Docling's existing structural/token chunker preserves headings and page provenance. PDFs include extracted text and page-image representations; images include native visual embeddings and available OCR. Unsupported formats remain downloadable with an explicit
```
unsupported
```
indexing status. Encrypted PDFs, unavailable model/OCR assets, malformed input, and extraction errors keep originals and report failures.
Jev organization is metadata, never a filesystem move. Full rebuilds prepare shared subject folders from headings, named projects and shared prose topics, then rank memberships with stored chunk embeddings and Jev. Subject paths provide parent/child navigation and descendant filters. Links preserve both endpoint versions and supplied evidence IDs. Judgments are validated against the offered choices and passages. Exact duplicate links are verified with SHA-256, independently of semantic neighbor rank; model passage similarity alone cannot label different files duplicates. Duplicate judgments never merge document identities. Candidate names exclude document types and test boilerplate. Project scope is retained for new topics as well as existing folders. Symmetric related/duplicate links display once per document/version pair; support and contradiction directions remain distinct.
Use a folder's action menu to delete its organization and move its documents to Unfiled, preserving their history. Use Document actions → Delete document to permanently delete a document and all versions after confirmation. A latest-version guard protects newer uploads from stale selections. Interrupted purges recover at startup; deleted identities cannot be restored by replaying an old upload request.

Symbiknow
File transfer client
```
uv run python client.py upload notes.txt photo.png
uv run python client.py upload notes.txt --document-id DOCUMENT_ID --expected-version v1
uv run python client.py download DOCUMENT_ID --version v1 --output-dir downloads
uv run python client.py search "What did we decide?" --evaluate
```
The client starts its own stdio server, so stop an existing server using the same data directory first. Prefer an agent's long-lived connection for background indexing. For a transfer-only session use
```
client.py --storage-only upload ...
```
. Use
```
--data-dir PATH
```
before the command for an isolated repository.
For retries across CLI invocations, pass one
```
--request-id UUID
```
per input file. Without explicit IDs, a fresh CLI invocation is a fresh upload.
The transfer client batches at most two small files per call and uses 256 KiB raw chunks for larger files, with SHA-256 verification and version-pinned downloads. It preserves filenames in metadata and prefixes downloaded filenames with document and version IDs to avoid collisions. It refuses to overwrite an existing output. Partial upload state is kept in
```
data/temp
```
; repeat chunks with the same request ID, offset, total size, and whole-file SHA-256 to resume. The default maximum file size is 256 MiB. Completed transfer receipts persist for idempotence.

Symbiknow
One Python application for local agent file memory. Original bytes and independent document histories live in an OCFL repository managed by
**rocfl 1.7.0**
, without Git. LanceDB holds two derived tables. Docling converts and chunks supported files;
**EmbeddingGemma 2**
embeds text and native images. Hosted
**TypeSafe Jev**
judges evidence and selects logical folders, groups, and versioned relationships.
The MCP server exposes exactly
**upload**
,
**download**
, and
**search**
. Files travel as base64 bytes through the official Python MCP SDK, including historical versions. An upload can be stored successfully while indexing is pending or has failed.

evidence.text:
Symbiknow
Sample tool arguments
Modes are
```
semantic
```
,
```
keyword
```
,
```
hybrid
```
, and
```
answer
```
(hybrid with Jev evaluation). Optional
```
folder
```
and
```
group
```
filters use logical metadata. Results identify the exact document and OCFL version, evidence IDs, passage/page provenance, score kind, and relevance explanation. Jev adds direct/partial/related/unrelated/uncertain judgments and IDs of supplied supporting passages. Pure visual matches have no text answerability claim. Jev may decline to assign a relationship.
